newsitem.title: USA: Duisenberg mum on European Central Bank post.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg mum on European Central Bank post.

text.p: Dutch Central Bank President Wim Duisenberg declined to comment on his prospects for heading the European Central Bank after introduction of a single European currency, slated for January 1999.

Duisenberg, scheduled in July to assume leadership of the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner to the ECB, was in Washington to deliver a speech at a U.S.-Dutch celebration of the 50th anniversary of the Marshall Plan.
"I am already to become the head of the European Monetary Institute," said Duisenberg, when asked about his chances for heading the ECB.
Asked how the selection process was likely to play out, Duisenberg responded, "I have not seen it playing out yet."
Duisenberg last month said he would like the job and has received an endorsement from German Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
France is reported to be pressing for one of its own nationals to be appointed president of the ECB and oversee the launch of the single currency, the euro.
